    10 Chicken Pasta Recipes You'll Actually Make

    Published: 10 Nov, 2026 | By Emilie Pullar

    Home / Pasta Collections

    Published: 10 Nov, 2026 | By Emilie Pullar

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:45
    Instaread

    If you’ve got chicken in the fridge and no idea what to do with it, I’ve got you. These are 10 of my favorite chicken pasta recipes, from a classic pesto chicken pasta to a cheesy tomato pasta bake and a cozy chicken gnocchi soup.

    If you’re new here, I’d start with my creamy chicken pasta. It’s a reader favorite for good reason! For a Sunday lunch when you’ve got a bit more time to cook, I’d go for my white wine chicken ragù.

    Hi! I don’t know how it works in your house, but in ours, I’m team creamy and my husband Dave is firmly team tomato. I’d go straight for the creamy chicken and mushroom pasta. If Dave’s choosing, I’d put money on the spicy tomato chicken pasta.

    I’ve included a mix of creamy and tomato based recipes, with a bit of everything in between. I’ve thoroughly tested them all in my own kitchen, but I love hearing how you make them your own. Toss in a handful of spinach or add an extra pinch of red pepper flakes if you like a bit more kick.

    01

    My best creamy chicken pasta

    If you’re new here, start with this one. Golden pan seared chicken and a creamy parmesan sauce make it the recipe I’d point you to when you’re craving a classic chicken pasta.
    25 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    02

    Spicy Tomato Chicken Pasta

    A rich tomato sauce with a kick of red pepper flakes. I love this one with rigatoni and a generous shower of parmesan cheese.
    35 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    03

    Creamy Chicken Pesto Pasta

    Bite sized pieces of golden chicken tossed through pasta in a creamy basil pesto sauce. A jar of your favorite pesto makes this an easy one to pull together on a weeknight.
    30 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    04

    Chicken and Mushroom Pasta

    If you love mushrooms, this is the one to make. Browning them first gives the creamy sauce a deep, savory flavor that is the perfect base for the creamy white wine sauce.
    35 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    05

    Chicken Pasta Bake

    Chicken and pasta in a creamy tomato sauce, baked under a layer of golden cheese. This is the perfect crowd pleaser and a great one to prepare ahead.
    1 hour 5 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    06

    Garlic Parmesan Pasta with Chicken (no cream)

    Tender chicken is tossed through a glossy garlic and parmesan sauce that’s packed with flavor, made without heavy cream but finished with plenty of cheese for richness.
    40 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    07

    Chicken and Chorizo Pasta

    Golden pan-fried chicken sits on top of a glossy, creamy tomato sauce infused with smoky chorizo, finished with just enough lemon to keep everything rich but balanced.
    40 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    08

    Chicken Ragu

    Chicken thighs are slowly braised with pancetta, white wine and herbs until meltingly tender, then shredded into the luscious, flavor packed sauce. Perfect with pappardelle pasta.
    2 hours 20 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    09

    Creamy Chicken and Bacon Pasta

    Crispy bacon, juicy chicken, and a silky parmesan cream sauce come together to make a dinner that feels indulgent but is completely weeknight friendly.
    40 minutes
    Make This Recipe
    10

    Chicken Gnocchi Soup

    And for a night when you’d rather have soup, this one has tender shredded chicken and pillowy gnocchi in a herby broth. Crusty bread for dunking is highly encouraged.
    50 minutes
    Make This Recipe

    Tips for the best chicken pasta

    • Try chicken thighs. Boneless, skinless thighs have more flavor than breasts and are more forgiving if you cook them a little longer. I love them for recipes where the chicken is cut into bite-sized pieces.
    • Give the chicken a light dusting of flour. When you’re pan-searing chicken, a little flour helps give it a golden crust. Shake off the excess before it goes into the pan.
    • Give the chicken room to brown. Pat it dry first and cook it in a single layer. If the pan is crowded, cook it in batches so it browns instead of steaming.
    • Use heavy cream for creamy sauces. It's the most stable cream for cooking. Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer and add a splash of pasta water if it gets thicker than you’d like.
    • Scoop out a cup of pasta water before draining. You probably won’t need it all, but a splash of that starchy water helps bring the sauce together. I like to leave the sauce a little looser in the pan because it thickens as it sits.
    • Finish the pasta in the sauce. For stovetop pasta dishes, cook dried pasta for about a minute less than the package says, then let it finish in the sauce. Toss it well so every bite gets coated.

    I hope you find a chicken pasta you love enough to make again and again. If you try one, let me know in the comments which one you went for!
